text_blocks.snippet: Colon cancer can be detected through various methods, including screening tests for those without symptoms, and diagnostic tests for individuals experiencing symptoms. Screening tests like colonoscopy, CT colonography, sigmoidoscopy, FOBT/FIT, and fecal DNA testing help identify precancerous polyps or early-stage cancer. If symptoms are present, colonoscopy, flexible sigmoidoscopy, or other imaging techniques like barium enema or MRI may be used to examine the colon and rectum.
